walkthroughs.body_html:
Paper 1: Shakespeare and Post-1914 Literature — a core area of GCSE English Literature.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Paper 1: Shakespeare and Post-1914 Literature brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Paper 1: Shakespeare and Post-1914 Literature.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is the dramatic function of a soliloquy?
options: A soliloquy is any long speech a character gives.
A sonnet must always be exactly ten lines long.
It reveals a character's inner thoughts directly to the audience while the character is alone on stage — a convention granting access to private psychology.
A soliloquy is when characters argue with each other.
A sonnet must always be exactly ten lines long.
Iambic pentameter is when every line rhymes.
Iambic pentameter is any line with ten syllables.
A line of five iambs (unstressed-stressed syllable pairs), creating a ten-syllable line with the rhythm da-DUM da-DUM da-DUM da-DUM da-DUM.

mcqs.q: What is the structure of a Shakespearean sonnet?
options: Fourteen lines in iambic pentameter, structured as three quatrains and a final couplet, rhyming ABAB CDCD EFEF GG, often with a volta near the couplet.
A sonnet must always be exactly ten lines long.
Iambic pentameter is when every line rhymes.
A sonnet is any short love poem.
